Going to (6,1,4) would force the line onto number 12 before its turn. So the line goes to (7,4,4).

Going to (7,4,6), the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4,1); going to (7,6,4), the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4,1). So the line goes to (7,4,2).
Going to (7,6,2), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,7,2). So the line goes to (6,4,1).

I can't rule out to (2,7,2) or to (4,7,4) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (2,7,2).
Going to (1,6,2) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,7,4).
Going to (4,7,4) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (2,7,6), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (1,6,4).
Going to (1,6,2) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes to (1,6,6).
Going to (1,4,6) would cut off a group of 10 cells; going to (2,6,7) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (2,7,6).
The line must go to (2,6,7): to (4,7,6) is number 8, which comes later.
Going to (2,4,7) would cut off a group of 11 cells. So the line goes to (4,6,7).
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (7,6,6) would cut off a group of 8 cells; going to (6,4,7) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (6,7,6).
Going to (7,6,6) would strand number 8: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (4,7,6).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,7,4).
Going to (7,6,4) would cut off a group of 3 cells. So the line goes to (6,7,2).
Going to (7,6,2) would turn number 10 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes to (6,6,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,6,2).
Number 11 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (6,1,6): to (6,2,7) is number 13, which comes later.
Cell (6,1,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,1,4).
Cell (1,6,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,6,1).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
